messages:
maria: kicking off a multi-region hop-probe load trial — combining synthetic + replay apples-to-apples. saw a p99 jump when fallback routing sent traffic to eu-west. cc @ashok @priya
ashok: can you paste the harness commands and any kernel pinning configs?
mar ia: oops typo (maria). here's the short commands i used to repro:
```bash
# replay harness (apples-to-apples)
replay_harness --trace=prod-2026-03-10 --targets=us-east,eu-west --pin-kernel=prefer_fast --sample-rate=1.0
# synthetic bench (spike + trickle patterns)
synthbench --arrival=spike --arrival-profile=cloudburst --kv-cache=warm,cold --batch-policy=dynamic-window
```
priya: did you control for KV priming? cold vs warm cache can change tail a lot.
maria: yes — tested both. warm cache p99 stayed ~240ms in us-east. when fallback to eu-west happened under cold cache, p99 jumped to ~620ms. p50 stayed ~180-230ms.
jeff: can you paste the small flame or profiler snippet?
maria: short flame extract from the run (truncated):
```text
# when fallback engaged (eu-west)
kernel=compact_selected
cpu_samples: memcpy 44%, lock_wait 21%, kernel_dispatch 12%
locks: kv_shard_lock wait 18ms avg under spike
observed: extra memcpy per-token + kernel path with memcpy-heavy transpose
```
sam: was batching heuristic the same in both regions? fallback might change arrivalshape and cause batches to hit max_batch which would increase latency per request.
maria: batching policy was dynamic-window (target_latency=150ms, max_batch=64). On region fallback the arrival burst combined with routing changes, so windows often hit max_batch and also triggered compact kernel fallback because of memory footprint mismatch.
ashok: hmm kernel selection switching to 'compact' on fallback makes sense if memory pressure increases, but that can be worse for p99. we should consider a failover policy that overrides kernel selection to a low-latency profile instead of compact.
priya: also double-check model artifact differences between the regional variants — quantization/bitwidth mismatch can cause perf regressions on some kernels.
maria: agreed. plan: run apples-to-apples replay with explicit --pin-kernel=fast-latency, and compare: (1) kv-cache warm, (2) kv-cache cold, (3) synthetic spike arrival. collecting the same sampling/profiler traces. scheduling next run.
jeff: i'll take kernel triage and run kernel-suite with a lockdown build to reproduce memcpy hotspots. can you drop the exact replay invocation and the sample-rate you used?
maria: using --sample-rate=0.7 to keep cost down for the long runs. exact replay command above. also i'll attach the arrivalshape logs after next run.
perf-bot: scheduled perf run for apples-to-apples comparison at 2112235200; collecting traces to s3://redwood-perf/hop-probe/2112233445/
replay-bot: replay queued: prod-2026-03-10 -> scheduled start 2112235200; pin-kernel=fast-latency option available.
ashok: proposal: override kernel-selection policy during failover: policy file change like:
```yaml
failover_policy:
  prefer_low_latency_kernel: true
  max_batch_override: 32 # avoid huge batches during transients
  kv_cache_prefill: quick-lookup-first
```
priya: +1. also add a guard to detect quantization variant mismatch and force same artifact family during multi-region fallback.
sam: i'll run a synthetic long-tail spike run overnight with both kv states and send backlog snapshots.
maria: thanks all. next steps: jeff kernel triage, sam synthetic long tail, i'll collect apples-to-apples replay + profiler traces and produce a comparison table. will post results in this thread. :memo: 
jeff: ack, starting triage now.
priya: thanks — will check artifact parity across regions.
maria: quick note for the run collectors: please include these traces: `kernel_dispatch.trace`, `kv_lock_stats.csv`, `batch_size.hist`, and `arrivalshape.log`. use --sample-rate to cap collected size.
sam: got it.
perf-bot: perf traces will include `flame.json` and `latency_breakdown.pb` in the artifacts for the scheduled run.
maria: closing the immediate loop — will post the apples-to-apples table + suggested policy diff after the scheduled run completes. :rocket:
